what_happened: The operator queued jobs A4–A9 as depending on the id of the first A3 job. A3 was rejected and re-asked under a new id. The plan still treated the dependency on the old id as met, so it ordered A4 first, before A3 existed. The operator's first fix request also named a file that does not exist, and that job (bdaq) was closed. The operator lowered the priority of A4 and A5 and queued a corrected plan fix.
cause: Dependencies are bound to a job id, and the plan reads any terminal state of that id as "met", not "landed and verified". A rejected or re-asked job leaves the old id terminal, and nothing links it to its replacement. Nothing resolves the dependency to the work itself, and nothing resolves file names in a request against the repo before the request is queued.
prevention: Make the planner and queue count a dependency as met only when the depended-on job has landed (verified and merged). A rejected, failed or closed dependency must hold its dependents. When a job is re-asked, record the link from the old id to the new one, and have dependents follow it or be held until the operator re-points them. Also resolve any file path named in a request against the repo at queue time and refuse or warn if it is missing.
proposed_request: Change plan and queue dependency handling so a job depending on another job id counts as met only if that job has landed. If the dependency is rejected, failed or closed, hold the dependents and say which id blocks them. When a job is re-asked, record the old-id to new-id link and make dependents follow it. At queue time, check that each file path named in a request exists in the repo, and warn or refuse if one does not. Acceptance: (1) a test where A3 is rejected and re-asked shows A4 is not ordered before the new A3; (2) a test shows a dependency on a closed job holds its dependents; (3) a test shows a request naming a nonexistent file is flagged; (4) existing plan tests still pass.
